problem: Deep-RL target-driven navigation such as Zhu et al. 2017 specifies the goal with a target image and uses scene-specific policies. It uses no semantic or relational knowledge about where objects tend to be. As a result, agents generalize poorly to unseen scenes and cannot handle target categories never seen in training.
motivation: Humans find objects in unfamiliar rooms using semantic and functional priors: mugs are in cabinets near the coffee machine, and an unseen fruit like a mango is probably in the fridge because apples are. Encoding such object-object relational priors, and grounding them in the current observation, should cut exploration and let knowledge transfer to novel scenes and novel target categories through their relations to known objects.
key_idea: Build an object-relation knowledge graph from Visual Genome, run a Graph Convolutional Network whose nodes combine a word embedding with the current frame's ImageNet classification scores, and feed the resulting per-node 'semantic prior' vector into an A3C navigation policy alongside visual and target-word features.
insight: The structure of the prior graph is what helps, not the extra capacity. In the kitchen ablation (no-stop, Table 3), SPL drops steadily as nodes or relations are removed (38.5 → 31.1 at 80% objects dropped, → 31.5 at 80% relations dropped). A fully-connected graph gives 32.5 SPL and a random graph gives 30.1 ± 0.6, both well below the Visual Genome graph's 38.5. The GCN adds only 0.12 GFLOPs on top of the ~4 GFLOPs A3C baseline. Gains are largest in seen scenes, including for novel objects, where the graph plus word embedding link unseen categories to known ones (with stop: seen/novel SPL 11.0 vs 5.7 for A3C). Gains are small in unseen scenes with the stop action (6.7 vs 5.7 SPL). Using typed edges ('on', 'next to') did not help, probably due to too little data per edge type. Training one model for all room types was worse than per-room-type models.
method: Visual branch: frozen ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 takes 224x224 RGB and outputs 2048-d GAP features. The current frame and 3 past frames are concatenated (8192-d), then FC+ReLU maps them to 512-d.
Semantic (target) branch: 100-d fastText embedding of the target category name, mapped by FC+ReLU to 512-d.

Knowledge graph: nodes are the 53 visible AI2-THOR object categories. An edge is added when any object-object relationship between two categories occurs more than 3 times in Visual Genome; edge types are ignored. Uses a normalized binary adjacency as in Kipf & Welling.

GCN for navigation: each node's input is the concatenation of FC-512(fastText word embedding of the node) and FC-512(ResNet-50 1000-class ImageNet scores of the current frame), giving 1024-d. Three GCN layers (1024, 1024, 1) produce a |V|=53-d semantic-prior vector, which FC maps to 512-d.

Policy: the 1536-d joint feature (visual + target + graph) goes into A3C with one 512-d FC+ReLU hidden layer, then policy and value heads. Actions are move forward, move back, rotate left, rotate right, and optionally stop.

Reward/training: +10 on reaching the target, -0.01 per step. Training uses RMSProp with lr 7e-4 decayed linearly, 20 threads on one Titan X, for 10M frames (no stop) or 25M frames (with stop). A separate model is trained per room type. Max episode length is 100 steps (200 for living rooms).

setting.backbone: ResNet-50 (ImageNet-pretrained, feature extractor) + fastText embeddings + 3-layer GCN + A3C actor-critic MLP (policy/GCN trained from scratch with RL)
setting.training_data: RL in AI2-THOR on 80 training rooms (20 each of kitchen, living room, bedroom, bathroom), known object categories only, 10M or 25M frames. Prior knowledge graph mined from Visual Genome (>100K images) object relationships. No human demonstrations.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (current frame + 3 past frames) + target category name (word embedding)
setting.action_space: discrete: move forward, move back, rotate left, rotate right, stop (a no-stop variant is also evaluated; step sizes not specified)
setting.privileged: none in the main (stop-action) setting. In the 'without stop action' setting the environment signals success and ends the episode (oracle stop).

numbers.extra: Unseen scenes, known objects. With stop action: success = within 1 m of and facing the target. 250 episodes per scene. Max 100 steps (200 living room). Separate model per room type; Avg is the mean over the 4 room types.

numbers_note: Benchmark is the paper's own AI2-THOR (iTHOR) object-goal split: 120 rooms, per room type 20 train / 5 val / 5 test, 53 target categories split into known/novel (Table 4). Unseen-scene rows are mapped to split 'test'. Seen-scene rows are mapped to 'val-seen'; the paper does not state which seen rooms are evaluated, most likely the training rooms. The Table 3 knowledge-graph ablation is SPL only, kitchen, no-stop; its 38.5 matches the unseen-scenes/novel-objects kitchen entry. In that ablation, fully-connected graph = 32.5 SPL and random graph = 30.1 ± 0.6. Training curves (SR/SPL vs iterations, 3 seeds) are given only in Figure 5.
results: Adding the Visual Genome knowledge graph via GCN beats the plain A3C baseline in every setting. With the stop action, averaged over 4 room types, SPL/SR is 46.0/56.7 vs 31.1/39.6 on seen scenes/known objects and 11.0/17.1 vs 5.7/9.9 on seen scenes/novel objects. The gap is smaller on unseen scenes: 6.7/13.4 vs 5.7/10.4 (known objects) and 3.1/8.5 vs 2.4/5.9 (novel objects). Without the stop action (oracle success), unseen scenes reach 34.5/56.9 (known) and 30.4/64.9 (novel) vs A3C 30.3/49.3 and 24.4/56.5. The model also converges faster during training.
limitations: No long-term memory or map (stated). Absolute performance on unseen scenes with a learned stop action is very low (6.7 SPL / 13.4 SR), showing overfitting to training scenes.
Evaluated only in small single-room AI2-THOR scenes with a separate model per room type. The novel-object test set is only 1-2 categories per room type, and edge/relation types are discarded.
No real-robot or cross-simulator validation. The easier no-stop protocol relies on the environment signalling success.
compares_to: A3C baseline (same architecture without knowledge graph)
